Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Procurement asked me to confirm one thing before we take the quote to legal: how does Redwood handle commit reconciliation and make-goods for hosted per-token usage? A few specific questions:

- If we commit to an annual volume with quarterly reporting, how and when are overages invoiced? Immediate monthly billing + quarter true-up?
- If we underuse vs our commit, do unused tokens roll forward or do we get credited? Any cap or expiration?
- Are there explicit make-good credits if platform outages prevent us from consuming tokens? If so, how are those calculated?

We're trying to map this into our procurement checklist and would appreciate an example showing a simple 4-quarter reconciliation.

Appreciate it—

Hi Sarah,

Thanks — great questions. I put together a short explainer and a worked example attached (Atlas_Commit_Schedule_v2.xlsx) that walks through a 50M-token annual commit broken into quarterly targets. High level:

1) Invoicing cadence and overages
- Monthly invoicing applies to actual usage. If you exceed the committed quarterly slice in a given month/quarter, those tokens are billed at the agreed overage/on-demand rate on your next monthly invoice.
- At the end of each quarter we run a reconciliation comparing cumulative committed tokens vs actual usage. If cumulative usage > cumulative commit, we'll invoice the delta at the pre-agreed overage price as part of the quarter close (this shows up on the quarter-end invoice).

2) Underuse (unused commit) and carry-forward
- Unused commit may be carried forward up to two subsequent quarters (i.e., rollover window = 2 quarters) to allow for seasonality.
- Any unused commit remaining after the allowed carry-forward window will default to: (a) be applied to future quarters within the same contract year if you agree, or (b) if not used by contract year-end, Redwood will issue a one-time service credit ("make-good") up to 10% of the unused commit as goodwill, unless the shortfall is the result of documented platform availability issues (see next section).

3) Make-goods and downtime concessions
- Make-goods are reserved for documented Redwood service incidents that materially prevented the customer from consuming capacity. If there is a verified outage > 2 hours affecting Atlas' ability to consume, we calculate a pro-rata credit against that quarter's committed value (formula in the attached sheet).
- For commercial negotiation, we can offer a standard 10% goodwill credit for first-year contracts (subject to executive approval) to help with adoption risk.

4) Example and paperwork
- See the attached spreadsheet for a worked example and line items that would appear on invoices.
- I've also attached a redline of the MSA that highlights the reconciliation language (Draft_MSA_redlines.pdf).

If that looks good, I can put a short clause into the quote and generate a DocuSign when you're ready.

Best,

On Tue, Jul 21, 2026 at 11:08 AM Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@atlashealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Rishi — quick clarifying Q: if we spike above a quarterly slice mid-quarter and are billed at on-demand, will the quarter reconciliation ever refund that overage back to match the annual effective rate, or is it always charged as overage and only future invoice credits apply?

Great question. Short answer: reconciliation is performed on cumulative usage vs the cumulative committed amount for the contract year. If the annual cumulative usage stays within the overall annual commit, we will (a) apply credits to offset earlier on-demand overage charges at quarter reconciliation time so the net billing reflects the annual commitment, or (b) if cumulative annual usage exceeds the annual commit, any prior credits are reversed and the customer is invoiced the net delta.

Concretely: if you spike in Q1 but come in under the annual commit by year-end, the overage invoiced in Q1 would be offset by the quarter/year reconciliation and appear as credits by the subsequent invoice cycle. That prevents double-charging for seasonal spikes.

Hope that helps — happy to walk through the attached example live if useful.

Rishi

Hi Sarah — following our internal approvals, confirming the proposed commercial language and next steps. Final terms below; I pasted the short clause into the quote and pushed DocuSign (link below).

- Annual commit: 50,000,000 tokens (split into four quarterly slices of 12.5M tokens).
- Invoicing: Monthly invoices reflect actual usage. Quarterly reconciliation compares cumulative usage to cumulative committed tokens for the contract year and issues credits/invoices to reflect the net delta.
- Overages: Any usage above the annual commit is invoiced at the pre-agreed overage rate (1.2x base per-token rate) on the quarter close.
- Carry-forward: Unused commit may roll forward up to two quarters. Unused commit remaining at year-end will be eligible for a one-time service credit up to 10% of the unused committed value unless a documented Redwood service incident prevented consumption.
- Make-good: We will provide a one-time 10% goodwill credit for the first contract year (applied as a credit on the first quarter-end invoice after signature). This credit is capped at 10% of the annual committed spend and excludes customer-caused configuration issues.

Attachments and links: DocuSign quote is available here: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/quote/atlas-2026 (DocuSign_Quote_Atlas_Health_2026.pdf attached). I've also attached the example schedule (Atlas_Commit_Schedule_v2.xlsx) and the redlined MSA for your counsel.
